english: He has lost his key.
korean: 그는 열쇠를 잃어버렸습니다.

english: Ow, I've cut my finger.
korean: 아야, 손가락을 베었어.

english: The road is closed. There's been an accident.
korean: 도로가 폐쇄되었습니다. 사고가 났어요.

english: Police have arrested two men in connection with the robbery.
korean: 경찰은 강도 사건과 관련해 남성 2명을 체포했습니다.

english: Where's your key? - I don't know, I've lost it.
korean: 열쇠 어디 있니? - 몰라, 잃어버렸어.

english: He told me his name, but I've forgotten it.
korean: 그가 나에게 이름을 말해주었지만, 잊어버렸습니다.

english: Is Sally here? - No, she's gone out.
korean: 샐리 여기 있나요? - 아니요, 외출했습니다.

english: I can't find my bag. Have you seen it?
korean: 가방을 못 찾겠어. 혹시 봤니?

english: James is on holiday. He has gone to Italy.
korean: 제임스는 휴가 중입니다. 그는 이탈리아로 갔어요.

english: Jane is back home now. She has been to Italy.
korean: 제인은 이제 집에 돌아왔습니다. 그녀는 이탈리아에 다녀왔어요.

english: Are you hungry? - No, I've just had lunch.
korean: 배고프세요? - 아니요, 방금 점심을 먹었습니다.

english: Hello, have you just arrived?
korean: 안녕하세요, 방금 막 도착하셨나요?

english: Don't forget to pay your electricity bill. - I've already paid it.
korean: 전기요금 내는 거 잊지 마. - 이미 냈어.

english: What time is Mark leaving? - He's already left.
korean: 마크 몇 시에 떠나니? - 이미 떠났어.

english: Has it stopped raining yet?
korean: 비가 이제 그쳤나요?

english: I've written the email, but I haven't sent it yet.
korean: 이메일은 다 작성했지만, 아직 보내진 않았습니다.

english: Have you traveled a lot, Jane? - Yes, I've been to lots of places.
korean: 제인, 여행 많이 다녀봤니? - 응, 많은 곳에 가봤어.

english: Really? Have you ever been to China?
korean: 정말? 중국에 가본 적 있어?

english: Yes, I've been to China twice.
korean: 응, 중국에 두 번 가봤어.

english: What about India? - No, I haven't been to India.
korean: 인도는 어때? - 아니, 인도는 가본 적 없어.

english: Have you ever eaten caviar?
korean: 캐비아를 먹어본 적 있나요?

english: We've never had a car.
korean: 우리는 한 번도 차를 가져본 적이 없습니다.

english: Have you read Hamlet? - No, I haven't read any of Shakespeare's plays.
korean: 햄릿 읽어봤니? - 아니, 셰익스피어 연극은 하나도 안 읽어봤어.

english: Susan really loves that film. She's seen it eight times.
korean: 수잔은 그 영화를 정말 좋아해. 8번이나 봤대.

english: What a boring film! It's the most boring film I've ever seen.
korean: 정말 지루한 영화네! 내가 본 영화 중 가장 지루해.

english: I've never been to China. Have you been there?
korean: 난 중국에 가본 적 없어. 너는 가봤니?

english: Have you heard anything from Brian recently?
korean: 최근에 브라이언한테서 무슨 소식 들었니?

english: I've met a lot of people in the last few days.
korean: 지난 며칠 동안 많은 사람들을 만났습니다.

english: Everything is going well. We haven't had any problems so far.
korean: 모든 것이 순조롭게 진행되고 있습니다. 지금까지는 아무 문제가 없었어요.

english: I'm hungry. I haven't eaten anything since breakfast.
korean: 배고파요. 아침 이후로 아무것도 못 먹었어요.

english: It's good to see you again. We haven't seen each other for a long time.
korean: 다시 만나서 반가워. 우리 오랫동안 못 봤잖아.

english: I've drunk four cups of coffee today.
korean: 오늘 커피를 네 잔이나 마셨습니다.

english: Have you had a holiday this year?
korean: 올해 휴가 다녀오셨나요?

english: I haven't seen Tom this morning, have you?
korean: 오늘 아침에 톰 못 봤는데, 너는 봤니?

english: Don is having a driving lesson. It's his first one.
korean: 돈은 운전 강습을 받고 있습니다. 이번이 첫 번째예요.

english: It's the first time he has driven a car.
korean: 그가 운전을 해보는 것은 이번이 처음입니다.

english: Sarah has lost her passport again. This is the second time this has happened.
korean: 사라가 여권을 또 잃어버렸어. 이런 일이 벌써 두 번째야.

english: Bill is phoning his girlfriend again. That's the third time he's phoned her this evening.
korean: 빌이 여자친구에게 또 전화를 걸고 있어. 오늘 저녁에만 벌써 세 번째야.

english: It has been raining. You're out of breath, have you been running?
korean: 비가 계속 내리고 있어. 숨이 차 보이는데, 뛰었니?

english: Paul is very tired. He's been working very hard.
korean: 폴은 매우 지쳤습니다. 아주 열심히 일해왔거든요.

english: Why are your clothes so dirty? What have you been doing?
korean: 너 옷이 왜 그렇게 더러워? 뭐 하고 있었던 거야?

english: I've been talking to Amanda about the problem, and she agrees with me.
korean: 아만다와 그 문제에 대해 이야기해 왔는데, 그녀도 내 의견에 동의해.

english: Where have you been? I've been looking for you everywhere.
korean: 어디 있었어? 널 사방에서 찾고 있었잖아.

english: How long has it been raining? - It has been raining for two hours.
korean: 비가 얼마나 오랫동안 내리고 있나요? - 두 시간 동안 내리고 있어요.

english: How long have you been learning English?
korean: 영어를 배운 지 얼마나 되셨나요?

english: Tim is still watching TV. He's been watching TV all day.
korean: 팀은 아직도 TV를 보고 있어. 하루 종일 TV만 보고 있다니까.

english: Chris hasn't been feeling well recently.
korean: 크리스는 최근에 몸이 별로 안 좋았어요.

english: Sylvia is a very good tennis player. She's been playing since she was eight.
korean: 실비아는 테니스를 아주 잘 칩니다. 여덟 살 때부터 쳐왔거든요.

english: Every morning they meet in the same cafe. They've been going there for years.
korean: 매일 아침 그들은 같은 카페에서 만납니다. 수년째 그곳에 가고 있어요.

english: Don't disturb me now, I'm working. I've been working hard.
korean: 지금 방해하지 마, 나 일하는 중이야. 열심히 일해왔단 말야.

english: We need an umbrella. It's raining. The ground is wet, it's been raining.
korean: 우산이 필요해. 비가 오고 있어. 땅이 젖었네, 비가 왔었나 봐.

english: Hurry up, we're waiting! We've been waiting for an hour.
korean: 서둘러, 기다리고 있잖아! 우리 한 시간째 기다리고 있어.

english: There is paint on Kate's clothes. She has been painting her bedroom.
korean: 케이트 옷에 페인트가 묻어 있어. 침실을 페인트칠하고 있었거든.

english: My hands are very dirty. I've been repairing my bike. Now I've repaired it.
korean: 손이 너무 더러워. 자전거를 수리하고 있었어. 이제 다 고쳤어.

english: Joe has been eating too much recently. He should eat less.
korean: 조는 최근에 너무 과식하고 있어. 좀 적게 먹어야 해.

english: Somebody has eaten all the chocolates. The box is empty.
korean: 누군가 초콜릿을 다 먹어버렸어. 상자가 텅 비었네.

english: Where have you been? Have you been playing tennis?
korean: 어디 있었어? 테니스 치고 있었니?

english: How long have you been reading that book? How much of that book have you read?
korean: 그 책을 읽은 지 얼마나 되었니? 책을 얼마나 많이 읽었어?

english: Lisa is writing emails. She's been writing emails all morning.
korean: 리사는 이메일을 작성 중입니다. 아침 내내 이메일을 쓰고 있어요.

english: Lisa has sent lots of emails this morning.
korean: 리사는 오늘 아침에 이메일을 많이 보냈습니다.

english: They've been playing tennis since 2:00. They've played tennis three times this week.
korean: 그들은 2시부터 테니스를 치고 있습니다. 이번 주에 테니스를 3번 쳤어요.

english: I've known about the problem for a long time.
korean: 저는 그 문제에 대해 오래전부터 알고 있었습니다.

english: How long have you had that camera?
korean: 그 카메라를 가지고 계신 지 얼마나 되었나요?

english: I've been meaning to phone Jane, but I keep forgetting.
korean: 제인에게 전화하려고 마음먹고 있었는데, 자꾸 깜빡하네.

english: They have been married for 20 years.
korean: 그들은 결혼한 지 20년이 되었습니다.

english: Paul is in hospital. He's been in hospital since Monday.
korean: 폴은 입원 중입니다. 월요일부터 계속 병원에 입원해 있어요.

english: Have you known each other for a long time?
korean: 서로 알고 지낸 지 오래되셨나요?

english: She's waiting for somebody. She's been waiting all morning.
korean: 그녀는 누군가를 기다리고 있습니다. 아침 내내 기다리고 있어요.

english: How long have they had their car?
korean: 그들은 차를 산 지 얼마나 되었나요?

english: I've been learning English for six months.
korean: 저는 영어를 6개월 동안 배우고 있습니다.

english: It's been raining since lunchtime.
korean: 점심시간 이후로 비가 계속 내리고 있습니다.

english: Richard has been doing the same job for 20 years.
korean: 리처드는 20년 동안 같은 일을 해오고 있습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: How long have you been driving? - Since I was 17.
korean: 운전한 지 얼마나 되셨나요? - 17살 때부터요.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: How long have you known Jane?
korean: 제인을 알고 지낸 지 얼마나 되었나요?

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: I've had a pain in my stomach all day.
korean: 하루 종일 배가 아픕니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: Julia has been living here for a long time.
korean: 줄리아는 오랫동안 여기에 살고 있습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: How long have you been working here?
korean: 여기서 일하신 지 얼마나 되셨나요?

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: I've always lived in the country.
korean: 저는 항상 시골에서 살아왔습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: I haven't seen Tom since Monday.
korean: 월요일 이후로 톰을 보지 못했습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: Sarah hasn't phoned for ages.
korean: 사라는 오랫동안 전화를 하지 않았습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: I've been waiting for two hours. I've been waiting since 8:00.
korean: 2시간 동안 기다리고 있습니다. 8시부터 기다리고 있어요.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: Sally has been working here for six months. (or since April.)
korean: 샐리는 여기서 6개월 동안(혹은 4월부터) 일하고 있습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: When did it start raining? - It started raining an hour ago.
korean: 비가 언제 내리기 시작했나요? - 1시간 전에 내리기 시작했습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 7: Time expressions review (For and Since)
english: How long has it been raining? - It's been raining for an hour.
korean: 비가 얼마나 오래 내리고 있나요? - 1시간 동안 내리고 있습니다.

english: When did Joe and Carol first meet? - They first met a long time ago.
korean: 조와 캐롤은 언제 처음 만났나요? - 오래전에 처음 만났습니다.

english: How long have they known each other? - They've known each other for a long time.
korean: 그들은 알고 지낸 지 얼마나 되었나요? - 오랫동안 서로 알고 지냈습니다.

english: It's two years since I last saw Joe.
korean: 조를 마지막으로 본 지 2년이 되었습니다.

english: It's ages since we went to the cinema.
korean: 영화관에 안 간 지 정말 오래되었습니다.

english: How long is it since Mrs. Hill died?
korean: 힐 부인이 사망한 지 얼마나 되었나요?

english: He has lost his key. (He doesn't have it now.)
korean: 그는 열쇠를 잃어버렸습니다. (지금 없습니다.)

english: They've gone away. They'll be back on Friday.
korean: 그들은 어딘가로 떠났습니다. 금요일에 돌아올 거예요.

english: It has stopped raining now, so we don't need the umbrella.
korean: 이제 비가 그쳐서 우산이 필요 없습니다.

english: I've repaired the washing machine. It's working okay now.
korean: 세탁기를 고쳤어. 이제 잘 작동해.

english: Mozart was a composer. He wrote more than 600 pieces of music.
korean: 모차르트는 작곡가였습니다. 600곡이 넘는 음악을 썼죠.

english: My mother grew up in Italy. Did you know that?
korean: 저희 어머니는 이탈리아에서 자라셨어요. 알고 계셨나요?

english: Somebody has invented a new type of washing machine.
korean: 누군가 새로운 형태의 세탁기를 발명했습니다.

english: Who invented the telephone?
korean: 누가 전화를 발명했나요?

english: Ow, I've burnt myself! - How did you do that? - I picked up a hot dish.
korean: 아야, 데었어! - 어쩌다 그랬어? - 뜨거운 접시를 집었거든.

english: Look, somebody has spilled something on the sofa.
korean: 봐봐, 누군가 소파에 무언가를 쏟았어.

english: It was very cold yesterday. Paul and Lucy arrived 10 minutes ago.
korean: 어제는 매우 추웠습니다. 폴과 루시는 10분 전에 도착했어요.

english: Did you eat a lot of sweets when you were a child?
korean: 어릴 때 사탕을 많이 먹었나요?

english: I got home late last night. I was very tired and went straight to bed.
korean: 어젯밤 늦게 집에 왔어. 너무 피곤해서 곧장 잠자리에 들었지.

english: What time did you finish work?
korean: 몇 시에 일을 마치셨나요?

english: Tom has lost his key. He can't get into the house.
korean: 톰이 열쇠를 잃어버려서 집에 들어갈 수가 없어.

english: Tom lost his key yesterday. He couldn't get into the house.
korean: 톰은 어제 열쇠를 잃어버려서 집에 들어갈 수가 없었어.

english: Is Carla here, or has she left? - When did Carla leave?
korean: 칼라 여기 있나요, 아니면 떠났나요? - 칼라가 언제 떠났죠?

english: I've done a lot of work today. I did a lot of work yesterday.
korean: 나는 오늘 일을 많이 했어. 어제도 일을 많이 했지.

english: It hasn't rained this week. It didn't rain last week.
korean: 이번 주에는 비가 안 왔어. 지난주에도 비가 안 왔지.

english: Have you seen Anna this morning? (or Did you see Anna this morning?)
korean: 오늘 아침에 안나 봤니?

english: Have you seen Tim recently? - Did you see Tim on Sunday?
korean: 최근에 팀 봤니? - 일요일에 팀 봤니?

english: I don't know where Lisa is. I haven't seen her.
korean: 리사가 어디 있는지 모르겠어. 보지 못했거든.

english: We've been waiting for an hour. (We waited for an hour.)
korean: 우리는 한 시간 동안 기다렸습니다.

english: Jack lives in Los Angeles. He has lived there for seven years.
korean: 잭은 로스앤젤레스에 삽니다. 7년 동안 그곳에 살아왔어요.

english: Jack lived in New York for 10 years. Now he lives in Los Angeles.
korean: 잭은 뉴욕에서 10년 동안 살았어. 지금은 LA에 살지.

english: I have never played golf. (I didn't play golf last summer.)
korean: 난 골프를 쳐본 적이 없어. (지난여름에 골프 안 쳤어.)

english: It's been a really good holiday. I've really enjoyed it.
korean: 정말 좋은 휴가였어. 진심으로 즐거웠지.

english: When Sarah arrived at the party, Paul wasn't there. He had gone home.
korean: 사라가 파티에 도착했을 때 폴은 거기 없었어. 이미 집에 갔거든.

english: When we got home last night, we found that somebody had broken into the flat.
korean: 어젯밤 귀가했을 때 누군가 아파트에 침입한 것을 발견했습니다.

english: Karen didn't want to go to the cinema with us because she'd already seen the movie.
korean: 카렌은 이미 그 영화를 봐서 우리와 함께 영화관에 가고 싶어 하지 않았어.

english: At first I thought I'd done the right thing, but I soon realized that I'd made a big mistake.
korean: 처음엔 내가 옳은 행동을 했다고 생각했지만, 곧 큰 실수를 저질렀다는 걸 깨달았어.

english: The man sitting next to me on the plane was very nervous. He hadn't flown before.
korean: 비행기에서 내 옆에 앉은 남자는 매우 긴장하고 있었어. 비행기를 타본 적이 없었거든.

english: Who is that woman? I've seen her before, but I can't remember where.
korean: 저 여자분은 누구시지? 전에 본 적은 있는데 어디서 봤는지 기억이 안 나.

english: The house was dirty. They hadn't cleaned it for weeks.
korean: 집이 더러웠습니다. 몇 주 동안 청소를 하지 않았었거든요.

english: Was Tom there when you arrived? - No, he had already left.
korean: 네가 도착했을 때 톰이 거기 있었니? - 아니, 이미 떠났었어.

english: Kate wasn't at home when I phoned. She was at her mother's house.
korean: 내가 전화했을 때 케이트는 집에 없었어. 친정어머니 댁에 있었거든.

english: When the boys came into the house, their clothes were dirty and one had a black eye. They'd been fighting.
korean: 아이들이 집에 들어왔을 때 옷은 더러웠고 한 명은 눈에 멍이 들어 있었어. 싸우고 있었던 거지.

english: I was very tired when I got home. I'd been working hard all day.
korean: 집에 도착했을 때 매우 피곤했어. 하루 종일 열심히 일했거든.

english: When I went to Madrid a few years ago, I stayed with a friend of mine.
korean: 몇 년 전 마드리드에 갔을 때 친구 집에서 묵었습니다.

english: We'd been playing tennis for about half an hour when it started to rain heavily.
korean: 테니스를 30분쯤 치고 있었을 때 갑자기 비가 세차게 내리기 시작했어.

english: Paul went to the doctor last Friday. He hadn't been feeling well for some time.
korean: 폴은 지난주 금요일에 병원에 갔어. 한동안 몸이 안 좋았거든.

english: At last the bus came. I'd been waiting for 20 minutes.
korean: 마침내 버스가 왔습니다. 20분 동안 기다리고 있었어요.

english: James was out of breath. He had been running.
korean: 제임스는 숨이 차 있었습니다. 뛰었었거든요.

english: It wasn't raining when we went out, but the ground was wet. It had been raining.
korean: 우리가 나갔을 때는 비가 오지 않았지만 땅이 젖어 있었어. 비가 왔었던 거지.

english: Catherine was sitting in an armchair resting. She was tired because she'd been working hard.
korean: 캐서린은 안락의자에 앉아 쉬고 있었어. 열심히 일해서 피곤했거든.

english: They have a new car. (or They've got a new car.)
korean: 그들은 새 차를 가지고 있습니다.

english: Lisa has two brothers. (or Lisa's got two brothers.)
korean: 리사는 남동생이 두 명 있습니다.

english: I have a headache. (or I've got a headache.)
korean: 나 머리가 아파. (두통이 있어.)

english: Our house has a small garden. (or Our house has got a small garden.)
korean: 우리 집에는 작은 정원이 딸려 있습니다.

english: He has a few problems. (or He's got a few problems.)
korean: 그는 몇 가지 문제가 있습니다.

english: We're enjoying our holiday. We have a nice room in the hotel.
korean: 우리는 휴가를 잘 즐기고 있어. 호텔 방이 아주 좋거든.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Lisa had long hair when she was a child.
korean: 리사는 어릴 때 머리가 길었습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Did you have a car when you were living in Paris?
korean: 파리에 살 때 차가 있었나요?

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: I didn't have my phone, so I couldn't call you.
korean: 핸드폰이 없어서 전화를 못 했어.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Do you have any questions? (or Have you got any questions?)
korean: 질문 있으신가요?

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Does she have a car? (or Has she got a car?)
korean: 그녀는 차가 있나요?

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: I don't have any questions. (or I haven't got any questions.)
korean: 질문 없습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Sometimes I have a sandwich for lunch.
korean: 가끔 점심으로 샌드위치를 먹습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Mark is having a shower at the moment. He has a shower every day.
korean: 마크는 지금 샤워 중이야. 매일 샤워를 하거든.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: I don't usually have a big breakfast.
korean: 저는 보통 아침을 거하게 먹지 않습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: What time does Chris have lunch?
korean: 크리스는 몇 시에 점심을 먹나요?

unitTitle: Unit 14: Have as an action verb
english: Did you have trouble finding a place to live?
korean: 살 곳을 찾는 데 어려움을 겪으셨나요?

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: She used to travel a lot. She used to go away two or three times a year.
korean: 그녀는 여행을 많이 다니곤 했습니다. 일 년에 두세 번은 떠나곤 했죠.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: I used to play tennis a lot, but I don't play very much now.
korean: 예전엔 테니스를 많이 쳤지만, 지금은 그리 자주 치지 않아요.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: David used to spend a lot of money on clothes. These days he can't afford it.
korean: 데이비드는 옷에 돈을 많이 쓰곤 했지만, 요즘은 그럴 형편이 안 됩니다.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: Do you go to the cinema much? - Not now, but I used to.
korean: 영화관 자주 가시나요? - 지금은 아니지만, 예전엔 자주 가곤 했어요.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: This building is now a furniture shop. It used to be a cinema.
korean: 이 건물은 지금은 가구점이지만, 예전엔 영화관이었어요.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: I used to think Mark was unfriendly, but now I realize he's a very nice person.
korean: 예전엔 마크가 불친절하다고 생각했는데, 지금은 참 좋은 사람이라는 걸 알아요.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: I've started drinking tea recently. I never used to like it before.
korean: 최근에 차를 마시기 시작했어. 전에는 결코 좋아하지 않았거든.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: Lisa used to have very long hair when she was a child.
korean: 리사는 어릴 때 머리가 아주 길었습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: We used to live in a small village, but now we live in London.
korean: 우리는 예전에 작은 마을에 살았지만, 지금은 런던에 살고 있습니다.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: There used to be four cinemas in the town. Now there is only one.
korean: 동네에 영화관이 4개나 있었는데, 지금은 하나뿐이에요.

unitTitle: Unit 15: Used to in the past
english: I used to live alone. (I am used to living alone.)
korean: 예전엔 혼자 살곤 했어. (난 혼자 사는 것에 익숙해.)
